assertion: The Department of Education is falsely reporting $4.6 billion in canceled student debt as overdue loans, impacting over 300,000 borrowers, advocates say.
independent_value: PPSL press release: 'PPSL estimates, based on publicly available data, that the Department is falsely reporting $4.6 billion of cancelled debt, impacting more than 300,000 people.'
reason: AskAmerica has no table covering federal student-loan discharge status or post-discharge credit-bureau reporting. The article accurately quotes PPSL's own figure, but that figure is PPSL's unaudited litigation estimate, not independently verifiable against any government dataset or ED publication found in this research.

assertion: A class action lawsuit claims borrowers with forgiven loans are still being reported as delinquent, harming their credit and risking wage garnishments; two borrowers filed suit against the Department of Education on Thursday (Sept 24, 2026) in the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia.
independent_value: Confirmed directly: PPSL press release names plaintiffs Mandy Woods (Ashford University, ~$65,000 borrowed, credit report showed $71,901 owed as of Aug 2026) and Jorge Cortes (ITT Technical Institute, credit report showed $21,586 owed as of Aug 2026), filed Sept 24, 2026 in D.C. federal court under the Fair Credit Reporting Act.
reason: Matches the primary source exactly; no AskAmerica table applicable to a specific lawsuit filing.

assertion: 1.5 million borrowers had $23.4 billion in loans forgiven from 2022 to 2025 through the Department of Education's group discharge program for borrowers who attended colleges accused of misconduct, and were told the relief was automatic with no further action needed.
warehouse_value: No matching table (search_catalog found no student-loan-discharge coverage)
independent_value: PPSL press release states the identical figures and language verbatim. Independently corroborated in scale by a Dec 4, 2024 Senate letter (Sen. Markey et al.) itemizing named ED group discharges since 2022 -- Corinthian $5.8B/560,000, ITT Tech $3.9B/208,000, Art Institutes $6.1B/317,000, Westwood $1.5B/79,000, Marinello $238M/28,200, DeVry $415M/1,800, CollegeAmerica $130M/7,400, plus unquantified Phoenix/Ashford/Minnesota School of Business discharges -- totaling over 1.2 million borrowers as of Oct 2024, consistent with reaching 1.5 million/$23.4B by Jan 2025.

sources.title: Sen. Markey et al. letter to Sec. Cardona re: borrower defense discharges, Dec 4, 2024

reason: Checkable claim, corroborated by two independent documents beyond the article itself.

assertion: The Department of Education declined to comment on the case Thursday.
reason: A reporter's account of a declined-comment request cannot be independently verified after the fact from any government dataset or public document; no evidence contradicts it.
